keyframe_review.note: 74,990 km2 against the infobox's 70,000 km2 (no year; ratio 1.07): the island without Northern Ireland, whose six counties are not in the shape. The Treaty Ports (British naval bases on the south and north-west coasts, occupied by the Royal Navy per the page; return date not on the page) stay inside the Irish shape.

74,947 km2, the same twenty-six counties; de Valera became President of the Executive Council in February 1932 with no territorial effect. The 3 December 1925 agreement left the border unchanged (Partition of Ireland page).
Same cells; the border with Northern Ireland is the county line fixed by the Government of Ireland Act in force since 3 May 1921 and confirmed by the agreement of 3 December 1925.

region.text: the twenty-six counties of the Free State

ledger.note: 1922: the Irish Free State is established on 6 December 1922 as a Dominion under the Anglo-Irish Treaty (signed 6 December 1921), comprising 26 of Ireland's 32 counties. Northern Ireland opted out the next day (an address to George V approved 7 December 1922, received on the 8th, Partition of Ireland page). [Reviewer eu-21-c, 2026-10-31: counterpart kingdom-of-great-britain (ends 1800) changed to united-kingdom, whose /ledger/19 loses the Free State in December 1922]

1937: the Constitution of Ireland, approved by plebiscite on 1 July 1937, takes effect on 29 December 1937; the state is named Ireland (Eire) and a President replaces the Governor-General. Cliopatria carries the continuation as a separate row, Eire, from 1938.

certainty.note: The land border is the county line of the Government of Ireland Act (in force 3 May 1921), confirmed by the Boundary Commission settlement of 3 December 1925 which left it unchanged; the Treaty Ports were British-garrisoned Irish territory.

notes: Page budget (1-2 pages) spent on the Irish Free State and Partition of Ireland articles. Wars: none listed; the Irish Civil War (1922-1923) and the Anglo-Irish War are not on the pages opened, so no event is dated from memory. The Treaty Ports (occupied by the Royal Navy; the page does not name them or date their return) are recorded in a keyframe note, not as an occupation pair, because the end falls after 1937 and no page gives it. The 'Northern Ireland' opt-out of 7 December 1922 is in the found event's note; the UK (kingdom-of-great-britain, which Cliopatria carries to 2024) should carry the matching loss. Eire is the successor row; a single Irish state would join both dossiers (the infobox name changed on 29 December 1937).
